claim.statement: On 1 May 2026, domestic financial reporting showed Iran's capital-market reopening was a controlled freeze rather than normalization: IBENA, citing the Securities and Exchange Organization, said real-estate funds and fixed-income/housing-bond tools would trade again from Saturday 12 Ordibehesht, but equity trading would remain stopped through the end of Monday 14 Ordibehesht; the same report said equity reopening required issuer disclosure with security-information constraints, while SNN/Vista said reopening also depended on the scope of government support packages and final coordination, and NourNews/Vista said the capital market would resume in a staged and controlled way.
claim.subject: Iran's capital market
claim.object: partly frozen with staged reopening limited to safer instruments

evidence.summary: IBENA reports real-estate funds and fixed-income/housing-bond tools resume from 12 Ordibehesht, but equity-market trading remains stopped through Monday 14 Ordibehesht; it also says issuer disclosure must consider security-information constraints.

Existing SNN/Vista source says the Securities and Exchange Organization chair described technical readiness but conditioned reopening on issuer transparency, government support-package scope, and final coordination.
NourNews/Vista says a joint Economic Commission, Central Bank, and Securities and Exchange Organization meeting put capital-market activity on a staged and controlled restart path.
Existing Shahrara source records the equity-market halt through Monday 14 Ordibehesht.

information_depth.rationale: Multiple domestic financial sources and existing KNB rows converge on the same halted-equities, partial-tools, conditional-reopening pattern.

claim.statement: On 1 May 2026, Fararu reported the free dollar at 177,910 tomans, near the 180,000-toman band, with a 14% weekly increase, 12% monthly increase, and 117% yearly increase, showing the rial had not stabilized even after the immediate 180k record; existing KNB rows also record the late-April 180k break and official/trade-dollar controls around separate exchange channels.
claim.subject: Iran's free dollar market
claim.object: near a high 178-180k plateau after a sharp weekly rise

evidence.summary: Fararu reports the free dollar at 177,910 tomans on 11 Ordibehesht with 14% weekly, 12% monthly, and 117% yearly increases.
Existing KNB source records the late-April free-dollar break through 180,000 tomans.
Existing KNB source records the commercial dollar crossing the 141,000-toman channel in the exchange center, showing separate official/trade-dollar controls.

information_depth.rationale: The source gives precise price movement, but street-liquidity depth and executed transaction volume remain unclear.

claim.statement: A 2 May 2026 follow-up did not confirm the rumored Aladdin/Ferdowsi/Tehran Bazaar strike: Exa exact searches for Aladdin, Ferdowsi, Bazaar, Saturday, strike, closure, and reopening did not surface source-near strike confirmation, while an xPool latest query over Bazaar/Aladdin/Ferdowsi/currency/stock-market terms emitted only 13 items and none formed a clean source-near strike or closure cluster.
claim.subject: May 2 Aladdin/Ferdowsi/Tehran Bazaar strike rumor
claim.object: unconfirmed in fresh Persian search and xPool sampling

evidence.summary: The source notes list the exact Exa searches and record that they did not return source-near May 2 Aladdin/Ferdowsi/Tehran Bazaar strike confirmation.
The xPool query completed 10 pages but emitted only 13 items, with general dollar/market commentary and no clean source-near strike or closure cluster.
Existing IranWire source records earlier security pressure in Aladdin and Ferdowsi, so the absence here is a May 2 confirmation check rather than proof that pressure ended.

information_depth.rationale: This is bounded negative evidence under blackout/noisy-search conditions; it lowers strike probability but cannot exclude local closures.

assessment.uncertainty: A direct trader video, guild statement, or source-near market report could overturn this quickly.

synthesis.title: Cracks in the Islamic Republic, v34 - market stress is managed freeze, not verified Bazaar strike
synthesis.summary: The thirty-fourth pass tests the May 2 Bazaar/Ferdowsi/Aladdin rumor lane and updates the financial-market crack. Fresh Persian Exa searches and a 13-item xPool latest sample did not confirm a renewed May 2 Bazaar or Aladdin/Ferdowsi strike. That lowers the probability of visible merchant collective action today, but it does not mean normalization. The clearer signal is institutional market control: equity trading remains stopped through Monday 14 Ordibehesht, while safer instruments such as real-estate funds and fixed-income/housing-bond tools resume with extended hours; reopening equities is conditioned on issuer disclosure, security-information constraints, government support packages, and staged/controlled coordination with the Central Bank and parliament. FX remains unstable rather than calm: Fararu puts the free dollar at 177,910 tomans, near the 180k band, after a 14% weekly rise. Net: the regime appears to be containing market stress by freezing price discovery and reopening only controlled segments, while the Bazaar strike trigger remains unproven.
synthesis.limitations: Negative strike evidence is bounded by search visibility, internet controls, and noisy X search. Stock-market rows show formal controls, not the eventual selling pressure once equities reopen. FX-price rows show posted prices and percentage moves, not street liquidity depth.

information_depth.rationale: The synthesis combines fresh Persian financial reporting, existing KNB Bazaar/currency rows, and a bounded xPool rumor test.

operations.rationale: The claim directly tests whether the May 2 Aladdin/Ferdowsi security-pressure reports and strike rumors became a verifiable market strike.
The lack of source-near confirmation supports the forced-quiet/containment side of the May 2-4 reopening question.
Controlled reopening and issuer-disclosure constraints update whether stabilization is occurring through market controls and information limits.
The 177,910-toman dollar after a 14% weekly rise updates the question of whether the rial is stabilizing or breaking lower.
The capital-market freeze is part of the broader May 2-4 market reopening test, even though it is not a physical Bazaar closure.

operations.reason: v34 updates the active read from basic-service stress to the current market test: fresh evidence still does not verify a May 2 Bazaar/Aladdin strike, but financial-market controls and FX pressure remain a high-signal crack.
